mainTopic: Returning a lost object between people under a נדר forbidding benefit: two versions of the dispute between רבי אמי and רבי אסי, each tested against the משנה's rule that payment goes to הקדש.
overview: The גמרא tests the dispute between רבי אמי and רבי אסי against the משנה's line that, where people normally get paid for returning a lost object, the payment goes to הקדש. In the first version, that line fits the view that one returns the object even when the owner's property is forbidden to the returner. It seems hard for the view that he does not return it then. The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about only one case: where the returner's property is forbidden to the owner. Then the גמרא brings a second version of the dispute with the reasoning flipped. Here one opinion dismisses the worry of פרוטה דרב יוסף as rare and forbids returning when the returner's property is forbidden to the owner. The other opinion allows it, since he is only giving back the owner's own object. The משנה's payment rule fits the second opinion. For the first opinion the גמרא ends with an unanswered קשיא.

steps.title: The משנה fits the lenient view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that payment goes to הקדש and shows that it fits the view that one returns the object even when the owner's property is forbidden to the returner.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: where people take payment for returning a lost object, the benefit goes to הקדש. This fits the view that the returner gives the object back even when the owner's property is forbidden to him. That is why the משנה says the payment goes to הקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. First it shows that the משנה's line fits one side of the dispute easily, so it can next ask about the other side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Say the owner's property is forbidden to the returner. Then a payment from the owner would be forbidden benefit for the returner. So the משנה sends that payment to הקדש, and this fits the view that he still returns the object in that case.

keyTerms.meaning: The benefit should go to the Temple treasury
It makes sense according to (opens a contrast)
The owner of the lost object
The one who returns the object

phrases.english: We learned: In a place where people take payment for it
the benefit should fall to the Temple treasury.
It makes sense according to the one who says
that even when the property of the owner of the lost object
is forbidden to the returner, he also returns it.
That is why the משנה teaches:
In a place where people take payment for it
the benefit should fall to the Temple treasury.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the earlier dispute of רבי אמי and רבי אסי against the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that one does not return the object when the owner's property is forbidden to the returner.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup: the הקדש rule fits naturally only in the case where the owner's property is forbidden to the returner.

steps.title: The משנה seems hard for the strict view
steps.stepSummary: According to the view that he does not return the object when the owner's property is forbidden to him, why would the משנה need payment to go to הקדש?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says that when the owner's property is forbidden to the returner he does not return it, why should the benefit go to הקדש?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks its real question. Under the strict view, the case where the returner gets forbidden payment never happens, so why does the משנה talk about הקדש?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this view, the only case where he returns the object is when the returner's property is forbidden to the owner. In that case the returner may take money from the owner. So the הקדש rule seems unnecessary.

phrases.english: But according to the one who says

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֶׁנִּכְסֵי בַּעַל אֲבֵידָה אֲסוּרִים עַל מַחְזִיר
phrases.english: that when the property of the owner of the lost object is forbidden to the returner
he does not return it,
why should the benefit fall to the Temple treasury?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the בשלמא/אלא challenge set up in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The strict view of the dispute.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the only case this view allows, the returner may take payment from the owner, so sending it to הקדש seems pointless.

steps.title: The משנה teaches only one case
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is only talking about the one case where the returner's property is forbidden to the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה teaches about only one case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The הקדש rule is about the case where the returner's property is forbidden to the owner, and that case fits the strict view too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that case, if the returner gives up his normal payment, the owner gets a free service, which is forbidden benefit. So the payment is set aside for הקדש. That way neither person benefits, and the rule has a job even under the strict view.
steps.confusionAlert: The הקדש rule here is not about the returner getting money from the owner. It solves the opposite problem: the owner would be helped for free if the returner gave up his payment.

phrases.english: It teaches about only one case.
phrases.notes: The one case is where the returner's property is forbidden to the owner.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the משנה to one case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The הקדש line seemed to require the case where the owner's property is forbidden to the returner.
steps.terutzMaskana: The line refers only to the case where the returner's property is forbidden to the owner, which both views accept.
steps.whatToRemember: Both views can explain the משנה's הקדש rule, because the rule can apply to the case where the returner's property is forbidden to the owner.

steps.title: Second version of the dispute, with the reasoning flipped
steps.stepSummary: Some teach the dispute between רבי אמי and רבי אסי differently. One says the returner gives the object back only when the owner's property is forbidden to him, because פרוטה דרב יוסף is uncommon. When the returner's property is forbidden to the owner, he does not return it, because that would benefit the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach it this way: רבי אמי and רבי אסי disagree. One said: the rule was taught only when the owner's property is forbidden to the returner, and we are not worried about פרוטה דרב יוסף because it is uncommon. But when the returner's property is forbidden to the owner, he does not return it to him, because he would be giving him benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of the same argument, in which the allowed case and the forbidden case are swapped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, the worry was that the returner benefits through פרוטה דרב יוסף. Here that worry is dismissed as rare. The new worry is the opposite: returning the object gives the owner a free service from the returner, so it is forbidden when the returner's property is forbidden to the owner.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who teach it (a different version)
רב יוסף's coin: the small gain from being exempt from charity while busy with a מצוה

steps.whyThisMatters: The two versions disagree about which side's benefit is the real worry, and so they disagree about which case allows returning the object.

phrases.english: There are those who teach it in this wording:

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי.
phrases.english: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi disagree about it.
One said: They taught this only

phrases.aramaic: בְּשֶׁנִּכְסֵי בַּעַל אֲבֵידָה אֲסוּרִין עַל מַחְזִיר,
phrases.english: when the property of the owner of the lost object is forbidden to the returner,

phrases.aramaic: וּמִשּׁוּם פְּרוּטָה דְּרַב יוֹסֵף לָא שְׁכִיחַ.
phrases.english: and the worry about Rav Yosef's coin is not common.
phrases.notes: רב יוסף's point: someone busy with one מצוה is excused from giving a coin to a poor person, so returning the object could save him that coin.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל נִכְסֵי מַחְזִיר אֲסוּרִים עַל בַּעַל אֲבֵדָה —
phrases.english: But when the returner's property is forbidden to the owner of the lost object,
he does not return it to him,
because he would be giving him benefit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second version of the dispute that steps 1–3 were analyzing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to one view in this version, he returns the object when the owner's property is forbidden to him, since פרוטה דרב יוסף is rare. He does not return it when his own property is forbidden to the owner, since that gives the owner benefit.

steps.title: The second opinion: returning is allowed even when the returner's property is forbidden to the owner
steps.stepSummary: In this second version of the מחלוקת, the other אמורא says the returner may give back the lost object even when the returner's property is forbidden to the owner. The reason is that he is only giving the owner back what already belongs to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one said: even if the returner's property is forbidden to the owner of the lost object, it is permitted to return it. When he gives it back, he is only giving him back something that is his own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second side of the מחלוקת in this second version. This opinion allows returning the object even when the returner's property is forbidden to the owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion (step 4) forbade returning in this case, because the owner would be getting a benefit from the returner. This opinion disagrees. Giving back someone's own object is not counted as giving him anything new, so there is no forbidden benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: The property of the one who returns the lost object
The owner of the lost object

phrases.english: And one said:
phrases.notes: This is the second of the two אמוראים, רבי אמי and רבי אסי. The first one's view was in the previous step.

phrases.english: Even if the property of the returner is forbidden
to the owner of the lost object, it is permitted.
For when he returns it to him,
he is returning to him something of his own.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַד אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ נִכְסֵי מַחְזִיר אֲסוּרִים עַל בַּעַל אֲבֵידָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second version of the מחלוקת that began in step 4 by giving the opposing opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may return a lost object even when the returner's property is forbidden to the owner, since returning a person's own object is not giving him new benefit.

steps.title: The משנה's payment rule fits the second opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: where people normally get paid for returning lost objects, the benefit goes to הקדש. It then shows that this rule fits the opinion that allows returning even when the returner's property is forbidden to the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: in a place where people take payment for returning lost objects, the benefit should go to הקדש. This works well for the one who says that even when the returner's property is forbidden to the owner, he returns it. That explains why the משנה needed the rule about such a place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. First it shows that the משנה's payment rule fits the second opinion well. Next it will ask how the first opinion can explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the second opinion, returning is allowed even when the returner's property is forbidden to the owner. So the משנה's special rule about payment has a real case to apply to. The word בשלמא ("granted") signals that a contrast with the other opinion is coming.

keyTerms.meaning: Property belonging to the בית המקדש
Granted, this works for (introduces a contrast)

phrases.english: We learned:
A place where people take payment for it (returning a lost object),
the benefit should fall to הקדש.
Granted, according to the one who says
even when the returner's property is forbidden
to the owner of the lost object, he returns it,
this is how he explains the case of "a place" where payment is taken.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the two opinions of the second version against the משנה, starting with the opinion that fits.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first opinion of the second version (step 4)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup: the משנה's payment rule has a clear case to apply to under the second opinion, which prepares the contrast with the first opinion.

steps.title: How can the first opinion explain the משנה's payment rule?
steps.stepSummary: Under the opinion that he does not return the object when the returner's property is forbidden to the owner, the גמרא asks how the משנה's rule about a place where payment is taken can be explained.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who said that when the returner's property is forbidden to the owner, he does not return it, how does he explain the case of a place where people take payment?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now challenges the first opinion. If returning is not allowed in this case at all, the משנה's payment rule would have to be about the other case, where the owner's property is forbidden to the returner, and there it does not seem to fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 showed that the משנה's payment clause has a real job in the case where the returner's property is forbidden to the owner. The first opinion of this version says no returning happens in that case at all. So under this opinion the clause can only be about the case where the owner's property is forbidden to the returner, and it is hard to see why the payment must go to הקדש there.

phrases.english: But according to the one who said
that when the returner's property is forbidden (to the owner),
he does not return it,
how does he explain the case of "a place"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בְּשֶׁנִּכְסֵי מַחְזִיר אֲסוּרִין, וְלָא מַהְדַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the בשלמא/אלא contrast set up in step 6 by attacking the first opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first opinion of the second version: no returning when the returner's property is forbidden to the owner
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's payment clause assumes returning happens in that case. This opinion forbids returning there, so the clause would have no case to apply to.

steps.title: The question stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that this is a real difficulty for the first opinion and offers no answer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it has no answer to the challenge against the first opinion and simply says "קשיא".
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bare "קשיא" means the question stands unresolved. It is weaker than "תיובתא", which would mean the opinion is fully refuted. The first opinion stays a weakened view, while the second opinion fits the משנה smoothly.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult, an unresolved question

steps.whatToRemember: In this second version, the משנה's rule that payment goes to הקדש fits the opinion that permits returning even when the returner's property is forbidden to the owner. For the other opinion, it remains an unanswered קשיא.
steps.confusionAlert: "קשיא" here does not mean the opinion is thrown out completely. It means the גמרא found a strong question it could not answer.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of step 7 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The first opinion of the second version is left with an unresolved difficulty from the משנה.
